lead.en: Twelve short modules on the ideas behind Traditional Chinese Medicine — in English and Chinese, with an honest look at the evidence.
lead.zh: 十二個短單元，帶你讀懂中醫背後的觀念：中英對照，並且誠實地看證據。

about.en: This is the overview course: read it straight through in about two hours, or one module at a time. Each module ends with key terms and a short check. If you want to go deeper on any idea, the main 中醫養生 series has more than a hundred lessons.
about.zh: 這是一門總覽課程：大約兩小時可以從頭讀到尾，也可以一次讀一個單元。每個單元最後都有關鍵詞和小測驗。想更深入某個觀念，主系列「中醫養生」有一百多課可以接著讀。

about.en: This course is for education only. It is not medical advice and does not replace a licensed doctor or 中醫師. If you are pregnant, take prescription medicine, or have a health condition, talk to your clinicians before changing anything.
about.zh: 本課程僅供教育用途，不是醫療建議，也不能取代有執照的醫師或中醫師。如果你懷孕、正在服用處方藥或有健康問題，任何調整之前請先和你的醫師討論。

title.en: What TCM Is — and How to Read It
title.zh: 中醫是什麼——以及怎麼讀它

tag.en: A two-thousand-year-old medical tradition, read with two lenses.
tag.zh: 兩千多年的醫學傳統，要用兩種眼光來讀。

blocks.en: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is a medical tradition with more than two thousand years of written history. Its foundational text, the Huangdi Neijing (黃帝內經, The Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic), was not written by one person. It was put together by many hands, roughly between the third and first centuries BCE, and it has been commented on, argued over, and revised ever since.
blocks.zh: 中醫是一個有兩千多年文字紀錄的醫學傳統。它的奠基經典《黃帝內經》不是一個人寫的，大約在西元前三世紀到前一世紀之間，由許多人陸續編成；之後兩千年，歷代醫家不斷為它作注、辯論、修訂。

blocks.en: Today it is practiced in clinics and hospitals across the Chinese-speaking world, and related traditions grew up in Korea (Korean medicine, 韓醫) and Japan (Kampo, 漢方). In Taiwan, licensed TCM physicians (中醫師) work alongside Western-trained doctors, many hospitals have a TCM department, and National Health Insurance covers TCM clinic visits.
blocks.zh: 今天，華人世界各地的診所和醫院都有中醫；韓國的韓醫、日本的漢方，也是從同一個源頭發展出來的。在台灣，有執照的中醫師和西醫並肩執業，許多醫院設有中醫部，健保也給付中醫門診。

blocks.en: Two lenses
blocks.zh: 兩種眼光

blocks.en: To read TCM well, you need two lenses at once. The first is the tradition's own logic: what its concepts mean and how practitioners use them. The second is modern evidence: what clinical research has tested, what held up, and what has not been shown. Mixing the two up is the most common mistake, in both directions. Some people dismiss the whole tradition because its theory sounds strange. Others treat every traditional idea as if science had already confirmed it.
blocks.zh: 要讀懂中醫，需要同時戴兩副眼鏡。第一副看中醫自己的邏輯：這些概念是什麼意思、醫師怎麼用。第二副看現代證據：臨床研究測試過什麼、哪些站得住、哪些還沒有證明。兩者混在一起，是最常見的錯誤，而且兩個方向都有：有人因為理論聽起來陌生就全盤否定；也有人把每一個傳統說法，都當成科學已經證實。

blocks.en: This course keeps the two apart. The main text explains what TCM says, in its own terms. The green What research says boxes tell you, as plainly as we can, where the evidence stands.
blocks.zh: 這門課把兩者分開。正文用中醫自己的語言說明中醫怎麼講；綠色的「研究怎麼說」方塊，則盡量直白地告訴你證據目前到哪裡。

blocks.en: Three ideas that make TCM different
blocks.zh: 中醫跟西醫最不一樣的三個想法

body.en: A TCM diagnosis names a pattern (證, zheng) in the whole person, such as "Spleen qi deficiency with dampness." Two people with the same Western diagnosis, say chronic insomnia, may be given different TCM patterns and different treatments. This approach is called 辨證論治: identify the pattern, then treat.
body.zh: 中醫的診斷是替整個人辨出一個「證」，例如「脾氣虛兼濕」。兩個西醫診斷相同的人，例如都是慢性失眠，可能被辨成不同的證，用不同的治法。這就叫「辨證論治」：先辨證，再論治。

body.en: When TCM says "Spleen," it means a set of functions — mainly turning food into usable nourishment — not the organ you dissected in biology class. Module 4 explains this; it is the key that unlocks almost everything else.
body.zh: 中醫說的「脾」，指的是一組功能，主要是把吃進去的東西轉化成身體能用的養分，而不是生物課解剖的那個器官。第四單元會說明這一點，它幾乎是讀懂其他一切的鑰匙。

body.en: The classics praise the physician who keeps people well over the one who rescues them once they are sick. Diet, sleep, emotion, and living with the seasons are treated as medicine, not as extras.
body.zh: 經典推崇的是讓人不生病的醫者，而不是等人病了才搶救的醫者。飲食、睡眠、情緒、順應四季，在中醫裡本身就是醫療，不是附加的養生小撇步。

blocks.orig: 是故聖人不治已病治未病，不治已亂治未亂。
blocks.en: Therefore the sage does not treat illness that has already arisen, but illness that has not yet arisen; does not put in order what is already in disorder, but what is not yet in disorder.
blocks.zh: 所以聖人不等病發生了才治，而是在還沒生病時就調理；就像治國不等亂了才治，而是在還沒亂時就防範。

src.zh: 《黃帝內經・素問・四氣調神大論》

blocks.en: What TCM is not
blocks.zh: 中醫不是什麼

items.en: Not a religion. It borrows words like yin, yang, and qi from Chinese philosophy, but you do not have to believe anything to study it.
items.zh: 不是宗教。它借用了陰陽、氣這些中國哲學的語彙，但學它不需要信仰任何東西。

items.en: Not a replacement for emergency care. A stroke, a heart attack, a broken bone, or a high fever in a baby needs a hospital first.
items.zh: 不能取代急診。中風、心肌梗塞、骨折、嬰兒高燒，第一步都是去醫院。

items.en: Not "natural, therefore safe." Herbs are active substances. Some are toxic, and some interact with prescription drugs (Module 11).
items.zh: 不是「天然的就安全」。中藥有藥理作用，有些有毒，有些會和西藥交互作用（見第十一單元）。

body.en: The evidence is very uneven, so it has to be judged one therapy and one condition at a time. Acupuncture for some chronic pain conditions has enough trial support that the UK's NICE guidelines say it can be considered. The malaria drug artemisinin came out of a fourth-century Chinese herbal text and won a Nobel Prize in 2015. But the theoretical frameworks — qi, meridians, the five phases — have not been found as physical structures or measurable quantities. They are best read as a traditional way of organizing clinical observation. In 2019 the World Health Organization added a traditional-medicine chapter to its disease classification, ICD-11, for collecting data; WHO states that this does not mean it endorses the treatments.
body.zh: 證據的強弱差別很大，只能一種療法、一種病症分開來看。針灸用於某些慢性疼痛，臨床試驗的支持足夠，英國 NICE 的指引說可以考慮使用；抗瘧疾藥青蒿素出自四世紀的中醫古籍，在 2015 年得到諾貝爾獎。但氣、經絡、五行這些理論框架，至今沒有被找到對應的實體結構或可測量的量，比較恰當的理解，是把它們看成整理臨床觀察的一套傳統方法。世界衛生組織在 2019 年把傳統醫學章節納入疾病分類 ICD-11，目的是蒐集資料；WHO 明白表示，這不代表它背書這些療法。

body.en: To practice as a 中醫師 in Taiwan you must pass a national licensing examination. Most TCM clinics accept your NHI card: herbal granules, acupuncture, and 傷科 (manual therapy for injuries) are covered, with a small copayment.
body.zh: 在台灣要當中醫師，必須通過國家考試。大部分中醫診所都收健保卡，科學中藥、針灸、傷科推拿都有給付，只需付少許部分負擔。

terms.en: treating what is not yet ill

takeaway.en: TCM is a complete medical tradition with its own logic. Learn that logic on its own terms — and check each specific claim against the evidence, one therapy at a time.
takeaway.zh: 中醫是一套有自己邏輯的完整醫學傳統。用它自己的語言理解它的邏輯，同時把每一個具體說法，一種療法一種療法地拿證據來檢驗。

deeper.title: Treating What Hasn't Happened Yet
What "Yangsheng" Actually Means

q.en: Who wrote the Huangdi Neijing?
q.zh: 《黃帝內經》是誰寫的？

opts.zh: 許多人在幾百年間陸續編成

opts.en: Sun Simiao, in the Tang dynasty

why.en: The Yellow Emperor is a legendary figure the text is framed around. The book was compiled by many hands, roughly in the third to first centuries BCE.
why.zh: 黃帝是書中假託的傳說人物。這本書是許多人大約在西元前三到前一世紀之間陸續編成的。

q.en: Two patients have the same Western diagnosis. Will a TCM physician treat them the same way?
q.zh: 兩位病人的西醫診斷一樣，中醫師會用同樣的方法治療嗎？

opts.en: Not necessarily — it depends on each person's pattern
opts.zh: 不一定，要看每個人辨出的證

opts.en: Only if they are the same age
TCM does not treat Western diagnoses
opts.zh: 中醫不處理西醫的病名

why.en: This is 辨證論治: treatment follows the pattern, so the same disease can get different treatments (同病異治).
why.zh: 這就是辨證論治：治法跟著證走，所以同一種病可能用不同治法，叫做「同病異治」。

q.en: When TCM talks about the "Spleen," it mainly means…
q.zh: 中醫說的「脾」，主要指的是……

opts.en: The anatomical spleen, which filters blood
opts.zh: 解剖學上過濾血液的脾臟

opts.en: A set of digestive functions: turning food into nourishment
opts.zh: 一組消化功能：把食物轉化成養分

opts.en: A spiritual center with no physical role
opts.zh: 一個和身體無關的精神中心

opts.en: The pancreas, under a different name

why.en: TCM organs are systems of function. The TCM Spleen governs "transformation and transportation" (運化) of food and fluids.
why.zh: 中醫的臟腑是功能系統。中醫的脾「主運化」，負責轉化、運送飲食與水液。

q.en: Which statement about the evidence for TCM is most accurate?
q.zh: 關於中醫的證據，哪一句最正確？

opts.en: Science has confirmed all of TCM
opts.zh: 科學已經證實了全部的中醫

opts.en: Science has disproved all of TCM
opts.zh: 科學已經推翻了全部的中醫

opts.en: It varies: some therapies have good support for some conditions, others do not
opts.zh: 因療法而異：有些療法對某些病症有不錯的證據，有些沒有

why.en: Evidence has to be judged therapy by therapy and condition by condition — acupuncture for chronic pain is not the same question as an herb for diabetes.
why.zh: 證據要一種療法、一種病症分開判斷：針灸治慢性疼痛，跟某種中藥治糖尿病，是完全不同的兩個問題。

q.en: Your friend has sudden chest pain spreading to the left arm. What should they do first?
q.zh: 朋友突然胸痛，痛到左手臂，第一步該怎麼做？

opts.en: Drink warm ginger tea and rest
Call 119 or go to an emergency room now
Book a TCM appointment for tomorrow

why.en: Possible heart attack. Emergencies go to the hospital first; TCM can have a role later, in recovery.
why.zh: 可能是心肌梗塞。急症一定先送醫院；中醫可以在之後的復原期再參與。

tag.en: Not mysticism, and not good versus bad — a language for describing balance.
tag.zh: 不是玄學，也不是善惡二分，而是描述平衡的一套語言。

blocks.en: The characters tell the story. 陰 (yin) first meant the shady side of a hill; 陽 (yang) meant the sunny side. Same hill, two sides, and which side is which depends on where the sun is. Yin and yang are not two substances. They are relational labels: anything can be called more yin or more yang compared with something else.
blocks.zh: 看字就知道。「陰」原本指山的背陽面，「陽」指山的向陽面：同一座山的兩面，哪一面是陰、哪一面是陽，要看太陽在哪裡。陰陽不是兩種物質，而是相對的標籤：任何東西都可以說比另一樣東西更陰或更陽。

blocks.orig: 陰陽者，天地之道也，萬物之綱紀，變化之父母。
blocks.en: Yin and yang are the Way of heaven and earth, the framework of the ten thousand things, the father and mother of change.
blocks.zh: 陰陽是天地運行的道理、萬物的綱領、一切變化的根源。

src.zh: 《黃帝內經・素問・陰陽應象大論》

blocks.en: Four relationships
blocks.zh: 四種關係

body.en: They pull in opposite directions and keep each other in check — heat checks cold, activity checks rest.
body.zh: 兩者方向相反、互相制約：熱制寒，動制靜。

body.en: Neither exists alone. Night only means something because there is day; activity needs the rest that makes it possible. A saying from many centuries later puts it: 孤陰不生，獨陽不長 — yin alone cannot give life, yang alone cannot grow.
body.zh: 誰也離不開誰。有白天，夜晚才有意義；活動需要休息來支撐。晚了許多世紀的說法是「孤陰不生，獨陽不長」。

body.en: When one grows, the other shrinks, like the length of day and night across the year.
body.zh: 此消彼長，就像一年之中白天和黑夜的長短變化。

body.en: At an extreme, each turns into the other. The longest day of the year is the start of days getting shorter. The small dots in the taiji symbol show the seed of each inside the other.
body.zh: 到了極點會互相轉化：一年白天最長的那天，正是白天開始變短的起點。太極圖裡的小圓點，就是對方藏在自己裡面的種子。

blocks.en: Yin and yang in the body
blocks.zh: 身體裡的陰陽

blocks.en: In TCM, health is a working balance between yang — the body's warming, moving, transforming functions — and yin — the cooling, moistening, nourishing substances that anchor them. When the balance tips, the tradition describes four basic patterns.
blocks.zh: 中醫認為，健康是陽與陰之間的動態平衡：陽是身體溫煦、推動、轉化的功能；陰是涼潤、滋養、把陽穩住的物質。平衡一旦傾斜，傳統上分成四種基本型態。

rows.en: feeling hot, red face, thirst, irritability, constipation
rows.zh: 怕熱、臉紅、口渴、煩躁、便秘

rows.en: feeling cold, heaviness, pain eased by warmth, watery stools
rows.zh: 怕冷、身重、得溫痛減、大便稀

rows.en: always cold, tired, pale, frequent clear urine
rows.zh: 長期怕冷、疲倦、臉色蒼白、小便清長

rows.en: hot palms and soles, night sweats, dry mouth at night
rows.zh: 手足心熱、盜汗、夜間口乾

blocks.en: Notice that yang excess and yin deficiency can both make you feel hot — but in TCM logic the cause is opposite. One is too much heat; the other is too little cooling. The first is "cleared," the second "nourished." This is why the tradition warns against self-treating from a symptom alone.
blocks.zh: 注意：陽盛和陰虛都會讓人覺得熱，但在中醫的邏輯裡，原因剛好相反：一個是熱太多，一個是涼潤不夠。前者要「清」，後者要「補」。所以傳統上提醒，不要只憑一個症狀就自己下藥。

body.en: Yin and yang are a way of classifying, not something a lab can measure. It is tempting to say yin-yang "is" homeostasis or the two branches of the nervous system; those comparisons can help a beginner, but they are analogies, not findings. Researchers have tried to link yin and yang patterns to body temperature, hormones, or metabolism, with mixed and small results.
body.zh: 陰陽是一種分類方法，不是實驗室能測量的東西。很多人喜歡說陰陽「就是」體內恆定、或自律神經的兩個系統。這些比喻對初學者有幫助，但只是比喻，不是研究結果。曾有研究想把陰虛、陽虛和體溫、荷爾蒙、代謝連在一起，結果不一致，差異也不大。

takeaway.en: Yin and yang are relative labels for two sides of one balance. In the body, the question TCM asks is not just "hot or cold?" but "too much of one, or too little of the other?"
takeaway.zh: 陰陽是同一個平衡兩面的相對標籤。在身體上，中醫問的不只是「熱還是寒」，而是「這邊太多，還是那邊不夠」。

deeper.title: Yin and Yang Are Not "Good" and "Bad"
The Four Relationships Between Yin and Yang
Excess Heat and Deficient Heat Are Not the Same Thing

q.en: The character originally meant…
q.zh: 「陽」字最早的意思是……

opts.en: the sunny side of a hill

why.en: 陽 was the sunny side and 陰 the shady side of a hill — a picture of relationship, not of two things.
why.zh: 陽是山的向陽面，陰是背陽面。這是一幅「關係」的圖，不是兩樣東西。

q.en: Which is more yang?
q.zh: 哪一個比較偏陽？

why.en: Active, warm, rising, daytime: all yang qualities.
why.zh: 活動、溫熱、上升、白天，都是陽的特質。

q.en: Hot palms and soles, night sweats, and a dry mouth at night fit which pattern best?
q.zh: 手足心熱、盜汗、夜裡口乾，最符合哪一型？

why.en: Classic yin-deficiency signs: not enough cooling and moistening to balance normal warmth.
why.zh: 典型的陰虛表現：涼潤不足，平衡不了正常的溫熱。

q.en: Why does TCM treat yang excess and yin deficiency differently, though both feel hot?
q.zh: 陽盛和陰虛都覺得熱，為什麼中醫治法不同？

opts.en: Excess is cleared; deficiency is nourished
One is mental, one is physical
opts.zh: 一個是心理，一個是生理

opts.en: Only a blood test can tell

why.en: In TCM logic the cause is opposite, so the treatment is opposite: clear the extra heat, or replenish the missing yin.
why.zh: 在中醫的邏輯裡原因相反，治法也相反：一個清掉多出來的熱，一個補足不夠的陰。

q.en: "The longest day of the year is when the days start getting shorter." Which relationship is this?
q.zh: 「一年白天最長的那天，就是白天開始變短的起點。」這是哪一種關係？

why.en: At its peak, yang begins to turn into yin —.
why.zh: 陽到了極點就開始轉為陰，也就是「重陽必陰」。

tag.en: Why "energy" is the wrong translation — and what qi does instead.
tag.zh: 為什麼「energy」是錯誤的翻譯，以及氣到底做了什麼。

blocks.en: Qi (氣) is usually translated as "energy," and that translation causes trouble. Energy, in physics, is a quantity you can measure and store. Qi is not a substance sitting in a tank. In TCM, qi is better understood as the body doing its work: moving, warming, defending, holding things in place, and transforming food and air into the body's own substances. When a TCM physician says your qi is weak, they mean those functions are running below full strength — not that a battery is low.
blocks.zh: 氣通常被翻成「energy」，這個翻譯帶來很多麻煩。物理學的能量，是可以測量、可以儲存的量；氣不是裝在桶子裡的東西。在中醫裡，氣比較接近「身體正在做的工作」：推動、溫暖、防禦、固攝、把食物和空氣轉化成身體自己的物質。中醫師說你氣虛，意思是這些功能沒有全力運作，而不是電池沒電了。

blocks.en: Many teachers now leave qi untranslated, the way English keeps karma and nirvana. This course does the same.
blocks.zh: 現在很多老師乾脆不翻譯，直接寫 qi，就像英文直接用 karma、nirvana。這門課也這樣做。

blocks.en: The five functions of qi
blocks.zh: 氣的五大功能

body.en: Moves blood and fluids, and drives growth and the work of every organ.
body.zh: 推動血液與津液運行，推動生長發育和各臟腑的活動。

body.en: Keeps the body warm. Cold hands and feet are often read as qi (or yang) not reaching them.
body.zh: 維持體溫。手腳冰冷，常被解讀為氣（或陽）到不了四肢。

body.en: Defensive qi (衛氣) guards the surface of the body against outside "pathogens" such as wind and cold.
body.zh: 衛氣守在體表，抵禦風、寒等外邪。

body.en: Holds blood inside the vessels, sweat and urine until the right time, and organs in place.
body.zh: 把血留在脈中，讓汗、尿適時排出，讓臟器維持在原位。

body.en: Turns food, drink, and air into qi, blood, and fluids, and turns waste into sweat and urine.
body.zh: 把飲食和空氣化成氣、血、津液，也把廢物化成汗與尿。

blocks.en: Where qi comes from
blocks.zh: 氣從哪裡來

body.en: What you are born with, said to be stored in the Kidney. You cannot add to it, only use it wisely.
body.zh: 與生俱來，藏於腎。無法增加，只能善用。

body.en: Extracted from food and drink by the Spleen and Stomach — the source you control most.
body.zh: 由脾胃從飲食中化生，是你最能掌握的來源。

body.en: Drawn in by the Lung with each breath.
body.zh: 肺從每一次呼吸中吸入。

blocks.en: Four ways qi goes wrong
blocks.zh: 氣出問題的四種情況

rows.en: tired, soft voice, short of breath on effort, sweats easily, catches colds often
rows.zh: 疲倦、說話無力、動則氣喘、容易出汗、常感冒

rows.en: distension that comes and goes, sighing, tightness in the chest or sides, worse with stress
rows.zh: 時脹時消、常嘆氣、胸脅悶脹、壓力大時加重

rows.en: a dragging-down feeling, prolapse, fatigue that is worse standing
rows.zh: 下墜感、臟器下垂、站久更累

rows.en: qi going the wrong way: burping, hiccups, reflux, nausea, coughing
rows.zh: 氣往反方向走：打嗝、呃逆、胃酸逆流、噁心、咳嗽

body.en: Notice the difference between deficiency and stagnation in yourself. Tired all the time, worse after effort, better after rest? That is the deficiency picture. Fine after a walk, worse after a frustrating meeting? That is the stagnation picture. In TCM the first is built up, the second is moved — rest helps one, movement helps the other.
body.zh: 觀察自己是「虛」還是「滯」。一直很累、一動就更累、休息就好一點？這是氣虛的樣子。散步完反而舒服、開完一場讓人煩躁的會就悶脹？這是氣滯的樣子。在中醫裡，前者要補，後者要疏通：休息幫得了前者，活動幫得了後者。

body.en: No instrument detects qi, and claims that a device can "measure your qi" should make you suspicious. Comparing qi to ATP or metabolism can sound scientific, but it is a loose analogy. What you can say is that the patterns TCM groups under qi — fatigue, breathlessness, frequent colds — are real experiences worth taking seriously, and some of them, like persistent fatigue, can have causes such as anemia or thyroid problems that need a blood test.
body.zh: 沒有任何儀器能偵測到氣；聲稱機器可以「測你的氣」的，要保持懷疑。把氣比成 ATP 或代謝聽起來很科學，其實只是鬆散的比喻。可以說的是：中醫歸在「氣」底下的那些狀態，像疲倦、喘、常感冒，都是值得重視的真實感受；其中有些，例如長期疲倦，可能是貧血或甲狀腺問題，需要抽血檢查。

takeaway.en: Qi is not fuel in a tank; it is the body at work. TCM asks two different questions: is there not enough of it (deficiency), or is it stuck or going the wrong way (stagnation, rebellion)?
takeaway.zh: 氣不是油箱裡的燃料，而是身體正在運作。中醫會問兩種不同的問題：是氣不夠（虛），還是氣卡住了、走錯方向（滯、逆）？

deeper.title: Qi Is Not "Energy"
The Five Jobs of Qi
Qi Deficiency and Qi Stagnation Are Not the Same Thing

q.en: Why do many teachers avoid translating qi as "energy"?
q.zh: 為什麼許多老師不把氣翻成 energy？

opts.en: Because qi is a measurable quantity like energy
opts.zh: 因為氣和能量一樣可以測量

opts.en: Because qi describes the body's functions, not a stored quantity
opts.zh: 因為氣描述的是身體的功能，不是儲存的量

opts.en: Because the word is too long
Because qi only exists in the lungs

why.en: "Energy" invites the wrong question — "how much qi do I have?" — as if qi were fuel.
why.zh: 「能量」會引出錯的問題：「我有多少氣？」好像氣是燃料一樣。

q.en: Which is NOT one of the five functions of qi?
q.zh: 下列哪一個「不是」氣的五大功能？

why.en: The five are propelling, warming, defending, containing, and transforming.
why.zh: 五大功能是推動、溫煦、防禦、固攝、氣化。

q.en: Which source of qi can you influence most from day to day?
q.zh: 哪一種氣的來源，你每天最能掌握？

why.en: Inherited qi is fixed at birth. Food qi depends on what and how you eat — every day.
why.zh: 先天之氣出生就決定了；水穀之氣看你每天吃什麼、怎麼吃。

q.en: Burping, hiccups, and acid reflux fit which pattern?
q.zh: 打嗝、呃逆、胃酸逆流，符合哪一型？

why.en: Stomach qi should go down. When it goes up, TCM calls it rebellious qi.
why.zh: 胃氣應該往下走；往上衝，中醫就叫氣逆。

q.en: A clinic offers a machine that "measures your qi." What's the most reasonable response?
q.zh: 有診所推出一台「測量你的氣」的機器，最合理的反應是？

opts.en: Be skeptical — no instrument has been shown to detect qi
opts.zh: 保持懷疑：沒有儀器被證實能偵測氣

opts.en: Only trust it if it is expensive

why.en: Qi is a functional concept. A device claiming to read it is selling certainty that does not exist.
why.zh: 氣是功能性的概念；聲稱能讀出氣的儀器，賣的是不存在的確定感。

tag.en: The key that unlocks the rest: what "Spleen," "Liver," and "Kidney" mean in TCM.
tag.zh: 讀懂其他一切的鑰匙：中醫的脾、肝、腎是什麼意思。

blocks.en: Early Chinese physicians did look inside the body, but the organ names in TCM came to stand for clusters of function observed from the outside: what happens when you eat, breathe, sleep, get angry, or grow old. So when this course writes "Spleen" or "Liver" with a capital letter, read it as "the TCM Spleen system," not the organ in an anatomy textbook.
blocks.zh: 古代中國醫家確實解剖過人體，但中醫的臟腑名稱，後來代表的是從外面觀察到的一群功能：吃飯、呼吸、睡覺、生氣、變老時身體發生了什麼。所以這門課寫大寫的 Spleen、Liver，請讀成「中醫的脾系統」，而不是解剖課本裡的器官。

blocks.en: The five zang organs
blocks.zh: 五臟

rows.en: governs blood and vessels; houses the mind ()
only the pump in your chest
keeps qi flowing smoothly (); stores blood
the liver's chemistry on a blood test
transforms and transports food and fluids (運化); keeps blood in the vessels
governs qi and breathing; spreads defensive qi to the skin; regulates water
rows.zh: 主氣司呼吸、宣發衛氣、通調水道

rows.en: stores essence (精) for growth, reproduction, and aging; governs water; grasps qi

blocks.en: Each zang organ is paired with a fu (腑) organ: Liver with Gallbladder, Heart with Small Intestine, Spleen with Stomach, Lung with Large Intestine, Kidney with Bladder. The fu organs are "hollow": they receive, pass along, and empty out. A sixth fu, the Triple Burner (三焦), has no single anatomical counterpart at all; it names the pathways of water and qi through the trunk.
blocks.zh: 每一臟都和一腑配對：肝配膽、心配小腸、脾配胃、肺配大腸、腎配膀胱。六腑是「中空」的，負責受納、傳導、排出。第六腑「三焦」在解剖上根本沒有單一對應的器官，它指的是水液和氣在軀幹中運行的通道。

body.en: If a TCM physician says your Kidney is weak (腎虛), it does not mean your kidneys are failing. It describes a pattern — perhaps a sore lower back, cold feet, waking at night to urinate. And the reverse matters even more: real kidney disease is found with blood and urine tests, not by pulse. If you have diabetes or high blood pressure, get those tests regularly, whatever your TCM physician says.
body.zh: 中醫師說你「腎虛」，不代表你的腎臟在衰竭，它描述的是一種證型，可能是腰痠、腳冷、夜尿。反過來更重要：真正的腎臟病要靠抽血、驗尿查出來，不是把脈。如果你有糖尿病或高血壓，不管中醫師怎麼說，都要定期做這些檢查。

blocks.en: Why the Spleen matters so much
blocks.zh: 為什麼脾這麼重要

blocks.en: Because food qi is the source you control every day (Module 3), the Spleen and Stomach are called "the root of later heaven" (後天之本) — the foundation you build after birth. Much TCM advice about warm, cooked, regular meals is really advice about protecting the Spleen. The tradition says the Spleen likes dryness and warmth and dislikes dampness and cold; that is why a large iced drink on an empty stomach is a classic thing TCM tells you to avoid.
blocks.zh: 因為水穀之氣是你每天能掌握的來源（第三單元），脾胃被稱為「後天之本」，也就是出生之後要自己打下的根基。中醫許多「吃溫的、煮熟的、定時吃」的建議，其實都是在保護脾。傳統說脾喜燥惡濕、喜溫惡寒，所以空腹灌一大杯冰飲，是中醫最常勸你避免的事之一。

body.en: The zang-fu system is a functional model that grew out of observation, philosophy, and centuries of clinical use. It does not line up neatly with modern organs, and nobody should expect it to. It is most useful as the shared vocabulary TCM physicians use to reason and talk about a patient — which is also why you need to learn it to understand what your TCM physician is telling you.
body.zh: 臟腑學說是從觀察、哲學和幾百年臨床使用中發展出來的功能模型，本來就不會和現代器官一一對上，也不該這樣期待。它最大的用處，是讓中醫師推理、討論病人時有共同的語彙；這也是為什麼你要學它，才聽得懂中醫師在對你說什麼。

takeaway.en: A TCM organ name is a label for a set of functions. Learn the functions, and the rest of TCM starts to make sense — but never use a TCM organ diagnosis in place of a blood test.
takeaway.zh: 中醫的臟腑名稱是一組功能的標籤。學會這些功能，其他部分就讀得通了；但千萬不要拿中醫的臟腑診斷代替抽血檢查。

deeper.title_zh: 腎為先天之本，陰陽之根

q.en: In TCM, the Liver's best-known job is to…
q.zh: 在中醫裡，肝最有名的功能是……

why.en: 疏泄: keeping qi, and with it mood and digestion, moving freely. The Liver also stores blood.
why.zh: 肝主疏泄，讓氣、連同情緒和消化都運行順暢；肝也藏血。

q.en: A TCM physician tells you that you have "Kidney deficiency." This means…
q.zh: 中醫師說你「腎虛」，這代表……

opts.en: A TCM pattern, not a diagnosis of kidney disease
opts.zh: 一種中醫證型，不是腎臟病的診斷

why.en: It names a pattern. Real kidney disease is found with blood and urine tests.
why.zh: 它是證型的名稱。真正的腎臟病要靠抽血、驗尿才查得出來。

q.en: Which organ pair is correct?
q.zh: 哪一組臟腑配對是正確的？

why.en: Liver–Gallbladder, Heart–Small Intestine, Spleen–Stomach, Lung–Large Intestine, Kidney–Bladder.
why.zh: 肝膽、心小腸、脾胃、肺大腸、腎膀胱。

q.en: Why are the Spleen and Stomach called "the root of later heaven"?
q.zh: 為什麼脾胃被稱為「後天之本」？

opts.en: They are the first organs to form
They turn daily food into qi and blood — the foundation built after birth
opts.zh: 它們把每天的飲食化成氣血，是出生後的根基

why.en: Inherited essence belongs to the Kidney (先天之本). Food, digested every day, belongs to the Spleen and Stomach.
why.zh: 先天之精屬腎，是先天之本；每天消化的飲食屬脾胃，是後天之本。

q.en: Which TCM organ has no single anatomical counterpart?
q.zh: 哪一個中醫臟腑在解剖上沒有單一對應的器官？

why.en: 三焦 names the pathways of water and qi through the upper, middle, and lower trunk.
why.zh: 三焦指水液和氣在上、中、下焦運行的通道。

tag.en: Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water: a map of how systems feed and check one another.
tag.zh: 木火土金水：一張彼此滋養、彼此制約的關係圖。

blocks.en: The five xing (五行) are often called the "Five Elements," but 行 means to move or to act, so many scholars prefer "Five Phases." They are not chemical elements. They are five categories for sorting how things behave: Wood grows and spreads, Fire rises and flares, Earth holds and nourishes, Metal gathers and contracts, Water sinks and stores.
blocks.zh: 五行常被譯成「Five Elements」，但「行」的意思是運行、作用，所以許多學者比較喜歡譯成「Five Phases」。它們不是化學元素，而是五種歸類事物行為的類別：木生長舒展，火上炎，土承載化育，金收斂，水下行閉藏。

blocks.en: Two cycles
blocks.zh: 兩種循環

body.en: Each phase nourishes the next, like a mother feeding a child: Wood → Fire → Earth → Metal → Water → Wood. Wood feeds fire; fire leaves ash, which becomes earth; earth yields metal; metal gathers water (think of dew on cool metal); water nourishes trees.
body.zh: 每一行滋養下一行，像母親養育孩子：木生火、火生土、土生金、金生水、水生木。木頭讓火燒起來；火燒完成灰，化為土；土中藏金；金屬表面凝結水氣；水灌溉樹木。

body.en: Each phase restrains another, so nothing runs away: Wood → Earth → Water → Fire → Metal → Wood. Roots break up soil; earth dams water; water puts out fire; fire melts metal; an axe cuts wood.
body.zh: 每一行制約另一行，讓系統不會失控：木剋土、土剋水、水剋火、火剋金、金剋木。樹根鬆動土壤；堤防擋住水；水滅火；火熔金；斧頭砍木。

blocks.en: A worked example
blocks.zh: 實際的例子

blocks.en: A classic strategy is called 培土生金, "bank up Earth to generate Metal." Someone with weak digestion (Earth, the Spleen) who also catches colds easily (Metal, the Lung) may be treated mainly by strengthening digestion, on the reasoning that the mother phase feeds the child. This is how the five phases are used in practice: as a way of reasoning about connections, so that a physician looks beyond the organ where the symptom appears.
blocks.zh: 有一個經典治法叫「培土生金」。一個人消化弱（土，脾），又容易感冒（金，肺），醫師可能主要從強化消化下手，理由是母行能滋養子行。這就是五行在臨床上的用法：一種推想臟腑關聯的方法，讓醫師不只盯著症狀出現的那個器官。

body.en: The five phases come from early Chinese cosmology, which sorted everything — colors, seasons, directions, musical notes — into fives. The medical correspondences (Liver with anger, Lung with grief, and so on) are part of that system, not results of experiments. It is true that research links chronic stress to digestive, sleep, and immune problems, so the general idea that emotions affect the body is well supported. But the specific pairings, such as "grief damages the Lung," have not been shown to work the way the theory says.
body.zh: 五行出自中國早期的宇宙觀，把顏色、季節、方位、音律等一切事物都分成五類。醫學上的對應，例如肝配怒、肺配悲，是這套系統的一部分，不是實驗得出的結果。研究確實發現長期壓力會影響消化、睡眠和免疫，所以「情緒影響身體」這個大方向有充分證據；但像「悲傷肺」這種特定配對，並沒有被證明真的如理論所說的那樣運作。

takeaway.en: The five phases are a relationship map. Their value in TCM is the habit of thinking in connections — what feeds this, and what is supposed to keep it in check?
takeaway.zh: 五行是一張關係圖。它在中醫裡的價值，是養成用「關聯」來思考的習慣：是什麼在滋養它？又是什麼本該制約它？

deeper.title: The Five Elements Are Categories, Not Chemicals
The Generating Cycle
The Controlling Cycle
Supporting One Element to Rescue Another
deeper.title_zh: 抑木扶土／培土生金／滋水涵木

q.en: Why do many scholars prefer "Five Phases" to "Five Elements"?
q.zh: 為什麼許多學者喜歡用 Five Phases 而不是 Five Elements？

opts.en: Because means to move or act, not a substance
opts.zh: 因為「行」是運行、作用，不是物質

opts.en: Because the word element is too short
opts.zh: 因為 element 這個字太短

why.en: They describe ways of behaving and changing, not stuff.
why.zh: 五行描述的是行為與變化的方式，不是物質。

q.en: In the generating cycle, which phase is the "mother" of Earth?
q.zh: 在相生循環中，哪一行是土的「母」？

why.en: Fire leaves ash, which becomes earth:.
why.zh: 火燒成灰，化為土：火生土。

q.en: In the controlling cycle, what restrains Water?
q.zh: 在相剋循環中，什麼制約水？

why.en: Earth dams water:.
why.zh: 堤防擋水：土剋水。

q.en: Which phase goes with the Liver, spring, and anger?
q.zh: 肝、春天、怒，屬於哪一行？

why.en: Wood: growth, spring, the Liver and Gallbladder, the eyes, and anger.
why.zh: 木：生長、春天、肝膽、目、怒。

q.en: What does 培土生金 suggest for someone with weak digestion who catches colds often?
q.zh: 對消化弱又常感冒的人，「培土生金」的意思是？

opts.en: Strengthen digestion (Earth) to support the Lung (Metal)
opts.zh: 強化消化（土）來支持肺（金）

why.en: The mother phase, Earth, feeds the child, Metal.
why.zh: 母行土滋養子行金。

tag.en: Your usual tendencies, according to the nine-constitution model — a mirror, not a diagnosis.
tag.zh: 依照九種體質的分類看看自己的傾向：是一面鏡子，不是診斷。

blocks.en: TCM pays attention not only to what is wrong today, but to the kind of body you have: the direction you tend to drift when you are tired, stressed, or eating badly. This is your constitution (體質, tizhi). Two people can catch the same cold and react quite differently, and TCM would say part of the reason is constitution.
blocks.zh: 中醫不只看你今天哪裡不舒服，也看你是什麼樣的身體：當你累了、壓力大、飲食不規律時，身體習慣往哪個方向偏。這就是「體質」。兩個人得了同樣的感冒，反應卻很不一樣，中醫會說，部分原因就在體質。

blocks.en: The best-known modern system was developed by Professor Wang Qi (王琦) of the Beijing University of Chinese Medicine. It describes nine constitutions and became a standard of the China Association of Chinese Medicine in 2009. Researchers assess it with a 60-item questionnaire. Most people are not one pure type; they have a main tendency and often a second one.
blocks.zh: 最有名的現代分類，是北京中醫藥大學王琦教授提出的九種體質，2009 年成為中華中醫藥學會的標準。研究上用一份 60 題的問卷來判定。大部分人不是單純一型，而是有一個主要傾向，常常還帶著第二個。

title.en: This is a reflection exercise, not a test
title.zh: 這是自我觀察練習，不是測驗

body.en: The checklist above is a teaching tool written for this course. It is not the validated research questionnaire, and it cannot tell you your constitution. Use it to learn the nine types and to notice your own habits. If you want an actual assessment, see a licensed 中醫師 — and if any of these signs are new, severe, or getting worse, see a doctor first.
body.zh: 上面的勾選表是為這門課寫的教學工具，不是經過驗證的研究問卷，也不能告訴你你是什麼體質。用它來認識九種體質、觀察自己的習慣就好。想要真正的判定，請看有執照的中醫師；如果這些表現是新出現的、很嚴重或越來越糟，請先看醫生。

blocks.en: Constitution is described as a starting point, not a destiny. In the tradition it shifts slowly with age, diet, sleep, climate, and emotional life — which is the whole reason TCM gives so much daily-life advice.
blocks.zh: 體質被看成起點，不是命運。傳統認為它會隨著年齡、飲食、睡眠、氣候和情緒生活慢慢改變，這也正是中醫給這麼多生活建議的原因。

body.en: The nine-constitution questionnaire has been tested for reliability and used in large surveys, mostly in mainland China, and some studies find links between types and conditions like metabolic syndrome. (Taiwanese researchers more often use a locally developed questionnaire with three types: yang deficiency, yin deficiency, and phlegm-stasis.) That is evidence that the questionnaire measures something consistent. It is not yet evidence that eating or living "for your type" improves health outcomes; good trials on that question are few.
body.zh: 九種體質問卷做過信度檢驗，主要在中國大陸用於大規模調查，也有研究發現某些體質和代謝症候群之類的狀況有關聯。（台灣的研究則較常用本土發展的問卷，分陽虛、陰虛、痰瘀三型。）這表示問卷量到的是某種穩定的東西；但還不能證明「照體質吃、照體質過生活」能改善健康，這方面的好試驗還很少。

takeaway.en: Constitution is your body's usual direction of drift. Knowing the nine types helps you understand TCM advice — but a checklist is not an assessment, and a new or worsening symptom is a reason to see a doctor.
takeaway.zh: 體質是身體習慣偏向的方向。認識九種體質能幫你聽懂中醫的建議；但勾選表不是判定，新出現或越來越糟的症狀，是該去看醫生的理由。

deeper.title: Reading Your Own Yin-Yang Balance

q.en: Who developed the nine-constitution model?
q.zh: 九種體質是誰提出的？

why.en: Professor Wang Qi of the Beijing University of Chinese Medicine; it became a CACM standard in 2009.
why.zh: 北京中醫藥大學王琦教授；2009 年成為中華中醫藥學會標準。

q.en: Always cold, prefers hot drinks, cold hands and feet. Which type does this describe?
q.zh: 長期怕冷、喜歡熱飲、手腳冰冷，描述的是哪一型？

why.en: Not enough warming yang.
why.zh: 溫煦的陽氣不足。

q.en: Oily face, breakouts, a bitter taste in the mouth, sticky stools. Which type?
q.zh: 臉容易出油、長痘、口苦、大便黏，是哪一型？

why.en: Dampness plus heat.
why.zh: 濕加上熱。

q.en: What can this course's constitution checklist tell you?
q.zh: 這門課的體質勾選表能告訴你什麼？

opts.zh: 你在哪些描述裡看到自己，作為學習的起點

q.en: According to the tradition, can constitution change?
q.zh: 依照傳統說法，體質會改變嗎？

opts.en: Slowly, with age, diet, sleep, climate, and emotion
opts.zh: 會，隨年齡、飲食、睡眠、氣候、情緒慢慢改變

why.en: A starting point, not a destiny.
why.zh: 是起點，不是命運。

tag.en: Every food has a "nature" and a "flavor" — and cooking changes both.
tag.zh: 每一種食物都有「性」和「味」，而烹調會改變它們。

blocks.en: A classical phrase says 藥食同源: medicine and food come from the same source. TCM draws no sharp line between the kitchen and the pharmacy; ginger, scallions, Chinese yam, and red dates all appear in classical formulas. The aim of eating well, in TCM terms, is to choose foods whose properties balance your body, the season, and the climate you live in.
blocks.zh: 古話說「藥食同源」。中醫不在廚房和藥房之間畫一條硬線：薑、蔥、山藥、紅棗都出現在經典方劑裡。照中醫的說法，吃得好，就是選擇性質能平衡你的身體、季節和居住氣候的食物。

blocks.en: Nature and flavor
blocks.zh: 性與味

blocks.en: Foods are sorted on two scales. Nature (性) runs cold – cool – neutral – warm – hot and describes the food's effect on the body, not its temperature on the plate: watermelon is cold even at room temperature, and ginger is warm even in an iced drink. Flavor (味) has five values — sour, bitter, sweet, pungent, salty — each said to act in a particular way.
blocks.zh: 食物用兩把尺來分。性從寒、涼、平、溫到熱，描述食物吃進去對身體的作用，不是盤子上的溫度：西瓜放在室溫下仍是寒的，薑加進冰飲裡仍是溫的。味有五種：酸、苦、甘、辛、鹹，傳統上各有不同的作用。

rows.en: rice, sweet potato, red dates, honey

blocks.en: Cooking and pairing change the picture
blocks.zh: 烹調與搭配會改變性質

items.en: Cooking warms. Stir-fried cucumber is less cooling than raw; stewing and roasting add warmth.
items.zh: 烹煮會讓食物變溫。炒過的小黃瓜沒有生吃那麼涼；燉、烤都會增加溫性。

items.en: Pairing balances. Crab (cold) is eaten with ginger; hot pot is balanced with cooling vegetables; cold tofu gets scallions and ginger.
items.zh: 搭配能平衡。螃蟹（寒）配薑吃；火鍋配涼性蔬菜；涼拌豆腐加蔥薑。

items.en: Season and climate matter. The same bowl of mung bean soup that suits a Taiwanese August is a poor choice on a cold January night.
items.zh: 季節和氣候很重要。同一碗綠豆湯，台灣八月喝很合適，一月寒夜喝就不太對。

items.en: Moderation is the rule. The tradition warns that too much of any one flavor harms its own organ — too much sweet burdens the Spleen.
items.zh: 適量是原則。傳統提醒，任何一種味吃過量都會傷到它所對應的臟，例如甜食太多會加重脾的負擔。

body.en: Taiwan's food culture is full of this thinking: 薑母鴨 and 麻油雞 in winter, 綠豆湯 and 青草茶 in summer, and grandparents warning you not to drink iced drinks during your period. Vegetarian versions work on the same logic — 麻油猴頭菇 and ginger-sesame noodles are warming without meat. Note that sesame-oil and rice-wine dishes are strongly warming; the tradition does not recommend them during a fever or a sore throat.
body.zh: 台灣的飲食文化處處是這種想法：冬天吃薑母鴨、麻油雞，夏天喝綠豆湯、青草茶，長輩叮嚀生理期別喝冰的。素食也是同樣的邏輯，麻油猴頭菇、薑絲麻油麵線，不用肉也很溫補。麻油、米酒料理的溫性很強，傳統上發燒或喉嚨痛時不建議吃。

body.en: The hot–cold classification is traditional knowledge, and books do not always agree — tomato, soy milk, and pork are listed differently in different sources. No lab test measures whether a food is "cold." For actual nutrition, standard guidance still applies: plenty of vegetables, whole grains, beans, and fruit, and less sugar, salt, and fried food. Notice that the TCM advice and the nutrition advice mostly point the same way. Where they seem to clash — say, "avoid raw salads" — you can keep the vegetables and simply cook them.
body.zh: 寒熱分類是傳統知識，各本書也不完全一致：番茄、豆漿、豬肉在不同來源裡歸類不同。沒有任何實驗室檢驗能測出一種食物「寒」不「寒」。營養方面，一般的建議仍然適用：多吃蔬菜、全穀、豆類、水果，少糖、少鹽、少油炸。你會發現中醫建議和營養建議大多指向同一個方向；看似衝突時，例如「少吃生菜沙拉」，菜照樣吃，煮熟就好。

terms.en: medicine and food share a source

takeaway.en: Three things are worth remembering: cooked is warmer than raw, pairing can balance an extreme food, and the right food depends on your body and the season.
takeaway.zh: 記住三件事就好：熟的比生的溫，搭配可以平衡性質偏激的食物，什麼食物合適要看你的身體和季節。

q.en: What does cooking generally do to a food's nature?
q.zh: 烹煮一般會讓食物的性質變得……

why.zh: 炒、燉、烤都會增加溫性。

why.zh: 甘味，例如米飯、地瓜，但要適量；甜食太多反而加重脾的負擔。

q.en: TCM says "avoid raw salads" for a cold-natured person. What fits both TCM and nutrition advice?
q.zh: 中醫說體質偏寒的人「少吃生菜沙拉」。哪個做法同時符合中醫和營養建議？

why.en: You keep the nutrition and follow the tradition's logic at the same time.

tag.en: The seasons, the day, and the famous "organ clock" — what is classical, and what is later.
tag.zh: 四季、一天，以及有名的「臟腑時鐘」：哪些出自經典，哪些是後來發展的。

blocks.en: The Neijing devotes a whole chapter (Suwen, Chapter 2) to living in step with the seasons. The principle is to go in the same direction as the season's movement: grow in spring, flourish in summer, gather in autumn, store in winter.
blocks.zh: 《內經》用一整篇（〈素問・四氣調神大論〉）講順應四季。原則是跟著季節的方向走：春生、夏長、秋收、冬藏。

blocks.orig: 夫四時陰陽者，萬物之根本也。所以聖人春夏養陽，秋冬養陰，以從其根。
blocks.en: The yin and yang of the four seasons are the root of all things. So the sage nourishes yang in spring and summer, and yin in autumn and winter, to follow that root.
blocks.zh: 四季的陰陽變化是萬物的根本，所以聖人春夏養陽、秋冬養陰，順著這個根本。

src.zh: 《黃帝內經・素問・四氣調神大論》

rows.en: go to bed late and rise early, walk outdoors, loosen up — don't bottle things in
rows.zh: 晚睡早起、到戶外散步、放鬆舒展，不要壓抑

rows.en: be active, sweat a little, eat lighter; don't sit in freezing air conditioning
rows.zh: 多活動、微微出汗、飲食清淡；別整天待在很冷的冷氣房

rows.en: protect digestion from dampness: cooked, light food; job's tears, adzuki beans
rows.zh: 防濕護脾：吃熟的、清淡的，薏仁、紅豆

rows.en: go to bed early and rise early; moisten with pear, white fungus, lily bulb
rows.zh: 早睡早起；用梨、白木耳、百合潤燥

rows.en: go to bed early and rise late, keep warm, conserve energy, eat warming food
rows.zh: 早睡晚起、保暖、保存體力、吃溫熱的食物

body.en: Taiwan's climate makes "late summer dampness" easy to understand: plum rains in May and June, then months of heat and humidity. Taiwanese households follow the 24 solar terms (二十四節氣) too, which divide the year far more finely than four seasons.
body.zh: 台灣的氣候讓「長夏濕重」很好理解：五、六月的梅雨，接著好幾個月的濕熱。台灣家庭也常跟著二十四節氣過日子，把一年分得比四季細得多。

blocks.en: The organ clock
blocks.zh: 臟腑時鐘（子午流注）

blocks.en: You will often see a "TCM body clock" that gives each of the twelve main channels a two-hour peak: Lung from 3 to 5 a.m., Large Intestine 5 to 7, Stomach 7 to 9, and so on around the day. Its roots are old — the Neijing already describes qi flowing through the channels in a fixed order, but gives no clock times. The two-hour clock appears in later acupuncture texts — for example Dou Hanqing's Zhenjing Zhinan (針經指南, Yuan dynasty, 1295) — and is often taught under the name 子午流注, a term that also covers older methods for choosing points by day and hour.
blocks.zh: 常會看到一張「中醫人體時鐘」，把十二經脈各配一個兩小時的旺時：凌晨三到五點肺經、五到七點大腸經、七到九點胃經，繞一整天。它的根源很早：《內經》已經講到氣按照固定的順序流經各條經脈，但沒有標出時刻。兩小時一格的時鐘，出現在後來的針灸書裡，例如元代竇漢卿的《針經指南》（1295 年）；今天常以「子午流注」之名傳授，不過這個名稱也包括更早一套依日期、時辰選穴的方法。

body.en: Daily body rhythms are real and important: the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to the discovery of the molecular clocks inside our cells, and hormones like cortisol and melatonin rise and fall on a daily schedule. But the specific two-hour windows of the organ clock have not been confirmed by research. Claims such as "the liver detoxifies between 1 and 3 a.m." or "waking at 2 a.m. means a Liver problem" are not supported. What the tradition and sleep science agree on is simpler: keep a regular sleep schedule, get morning light, and avoid heavy meals late at night. If you regularly wake in the night, that is worth discussing with a doctor.
body.zh: 人體的晝夜節律確實存在而且重要：2017 年諾貝爾生理醫學獎頒給了細胞內分子時鐘的發現，皮質醇、褪黑激素等荷爾蒙也照著一天的時間表起落。但臟腑時鐘那些特定的兩小時區段，並沒有得到研究證實。「肝在凌晨一到三點排毒」「半夜兩點醒來代表肝有問題」這類說法都缺乏根據。傳統和睡眠科學真正一致的地方比較單純：作息規律、早上曬太陽、晚上別吃太撐。如果你經常半夜醒來，值得和醫生談一談。

terms.en: living in accord with the seasons

takeaway.en: Live in the direction of the season, keep a regular sleep schedule, and enjoy the organ clock as a piece of tradition — not as a diagnostic tool.
takeaway.zh: 順著季節的方向生活、作息規律；把臟腑時鐘當成一段傳統來欣賞，不要拿來自我診斷。

why.zh: 長夏。台灣梅雨和濕熱的月份，很容易體會。

Modern science has confirmed each two-hour window

opts.zh: 它是後來發展的；特定區段沒有研究證實

q.en: What do TCM and sleep science agree on?

opts.zh: 作息規律、早晨曬太陽、晚上不吃太撐

opts.en: Waking at 2 a.m. means liver disease
opts.zh: 半夜兩點醒來代表肝病

why.en: Simple, shared ground — and that is the part worth practicing.
why.zh: 這是兩邊共同的基礎，也是最值得實踐的部分。

tag.en: A map of connections — and five points you can press yourself.
tag.zh: 一張連結全身的地圖，以及五個可以自己按的穴位。

blocks.en: Meridians, or channels (經絡, jingluo), are the pathways along which TCM says qi and blood circulate, linking the surface of the body to the organs inside. There are twelve principal channels, each named for an organ, plus eight "extraordinary vessels" — the best known are the Governing Vessel (督脈) up the spine and the Conception Vessel (任脈) down the front midline.
blocks.zh: 經絡是中醫認為氣血運行的通道，把體表和體內的臟腑連在一起。主要有十二正經，各以一個臟腑命名；另有奇經八脈，最有名的是沿著背脊上行的督脈，和沿著身體前正中線的任脈。

blocks.en: Along the channels lie the acupuncture points (穴位). In 2008 the World Health Organization published standard locations for 361 of them, using codes like LI4 (Large Intestine 4) and ST36 (Stomach 36), so that practitioners and researchers around the world mean the same spot.
blocks.zh: 經絡上分布著穴位。世界衛生組織在 2008 年公布了 361 個穴位的標準定位，用 LI4（大腸經第 4 穴）、ST36（胃經第 36 穴）這類代碼，讓全世界的醫師和研究者說的是同一個位置。

rows.zh: 手少陰心經 HT・手厥陰心包經 PC

rows.en: Small Intestine SI · Triple Burner TE
rows.zh: 手太陽小腸經 SI・手少陽三焦經 TE

cap.en: Fire has two pairs, which is how five phases become twelve channels.
cap.zh: 火有兩對，五行就這樣變成十二經。

blocks.en: Five points worth knowing
blocks.zh: 值得認識的五個穴位

blocks.en: Acupressure — firm pressure with a thumb or fingertip — is the self-care version of acupuncture. Press straight into the point for 30 to 60 seconds, or rub in small circles for a minute or two, firmly enough to feel a dull ache but not sharp pain. Do both sides. The traditional unit of measurement is the cun (寸), based on your own body: the width of four fingers held together is about 3 cun.
blocks.zh: 指壓是針灸的自我保健版：用拇指或指腹穩穩地往穴位按 30 到 60 秒，或小圈揉一兩分鐘，力道以感到痠脹、不刺痛為準，左右兩側都按。傳統的量法用「寸」，以自己的身體為準：四指併攏的寬度大約是 3 寸。

body.en: Do not press on broken skin, bruises, varicose veins, swelling, or a recent surgical site. In pregnancy, LI4 and SP6 are traditionally avoided; if you are pregnant, skip self-acupressure unless a qualified practitioner has shown you what is safe. Pain that is severe, new, or getting worse is a reason to see a doctor, not to press harder.
body.zh: 破皮、瘀青、靜脈曲張、腫脹處，以及剛開過刀的部位都不要按。懷孕時，傳統上避開合谷（LI4）和三陰交（SP6）；懷孕的人除非有合格醫師教過你哪些安全，否則不要自己做指壓。疼痛很劇烈、是新出現的或越來越嚴重，該做的是看醫生，不是按得更用力。

body.en: No dissection or imaging has found meridians as physical channels. Researchers have proposed links to nerves, fascia, and blood vessels, but these remain hypotheses. For points, the best-supported example is PC6 (Neiguan) on the inner wrist: a Cochrane review found that stimulating it, including by acupressure wristbands, reduces nausea and vomiting after surgery, though it rated the evidence against sham treatment as low quality. For most other self-acupressure uses, the evidence is limited — though pressing a point is very low-risk.
body.zh: 解剖和影像都沒有找到作為實體管道的經絡。研究者提出過和神經、筋膜、血管有關的假說，但都還只是假說。穴位方面，證據最好的例子是手腕內側的內關（PC6）：Cochrane 系統性回顧發現，刺激內關（包括指壓腕帶）能減少手術後的噁心嘔吐，不過和假治療相比的證據品質被評為低。其他大部分的自我指壓用途證據有限，不過按穴位的風險很低。

takeaway.en: Meridians are a map of connections, not anatomy you can dissect. Five points and a minute of firm pressure are a real, low-risk self-care skill.
takeaway.zh: 經絡是一張關聯的地圖，不是可以解剖出來的構造。認得五個穴位、每次穩穩按一分鐘，是真實又低風險的自我保健技巧。

why.zh: Cochrane 回顧發現，刺激內關能減少手術後的噁心嘔吐。

q.en: Which points are traditionally avoided in pregnancy?
q.zh: 傳統上懷孕時避開哪些穴位？

why.en: LI4 (Hegu) and SP6 (Sanyinjiao).
why.zh: 合谷（LI4）和三陰交（SP6）。

tag.en: What a session is like, what the evidence shows, and what to tell your practitioner.
tag.zh: 看診是什麼樣子、證據顯示什麼，以及該告訴醫師哪些事。

blocks.en: The Chinese word 針灸 (zhenjiu) joins two therapies: 針, needling, and 灸, moxibustion — warming a point with burning mugwort (艾草). Modern acupuncture needles are nothing like injection needles. They are solid, flexible, and very thin (roughly 0.16 to 0.30 mm), sterile, and used once. Most people feel a brief prick, then a dull, heavy, or spreading ache called de qi (得氣).
blocks.zh: 「針灸」包含兩種療法：「針」是扎針，「灸」是用點燃的艾草溫熱穴位。現代針灸針和打針的針完全不同：實心、有彈性、非常細（大約 0.16 到 0.30 公釐），無菌、用一次就丟。大部分人只感到短暫的刺一下，接著是痠、脹、重或擴散的感覺，叫做「得氣」。

blocks.en: What a session looks like
blocks.zh: 看診的流程

items.en: Assessment. Questions about your history, sleep, and digestion; looking at your tongue; feeling the pulse at both wrists.
items.zh: 四診。問病史、睡眠、消化；看舌頭；把兩手的脈。

items.en: Needling. Usually several to a dozen or more needles, chosen for your pattern, sometimes far from where it hurts.
items.zh: 下針。依照你的證型選穴，通常幾針到十幾針，有時扎在離痛處很遠的地方。

items.en: Retention. You rest for 15 to 30 minutes; many people find it relaxing.
items.zh: 留針。躺著休息 15 到 30 分鐘，很多人覺得很放鬆。

items.en: A course of treatment. A fair trial for a long-standing problem is usually several sessions over some weeks. If nothing changes, reassess.
items.zh: 療程。長期的問題通常要在幾週內做幾次，才算公平的嘗試；如果都沒有變化，就要重新評估。

blocks.en: Related therapies
blocks.zh: 相關療法

body.en: Burning mugwort near the skin to warm a point, used especially for "cold" patterns. Burns are the main risk.
body.zh: 在皮膚附近燃燒艾草溫熱穴位，特別用於寒證。主要風險是燙傷。

body.en: Cups create suction on the skin. The round marks last several days and are bruises, not "toxins coming out."
body.zh: 用罐子在皮膚上產生吸力。留下的圓形痕跡會持續幾天，那是瘀血，不是「毒素排出來」。

body.en: Scraping the skin with a smooth tool until red marks appear.
body.zh: 用光滑的工具刮皮膚，直到出現紅色痧痕。

body.en: Chinese therapeutic massage. In Taiwan, injury-related manual therapy is called 傷科.
body.zh: 中醫治療性按摩。在台灣，處理跌打損傷的手法治療稱為「傷科」。

body.en: Acupuncture is one of the most studied parts of TCM. The UK's NICE guidelines say acupuncture can be considered for chronic primary pain and for preventing chronic tension-type headache (and migraine, if standard preventive drugs have not worked), and the US National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health summarizes evidence that it may help low-back pain, neck pain, knee osteoarthritis, and headaches. Guidelines do not always agree: NICE's own low-back-pain guideline says not to offer it. Two more honest caveats: in many trials, "sham" acupuncture (fake or shallow needling) does nearly as well as the real thing, so how much of the benefit comes from the specific points is debated; and for many other conditions — including fertility, where a large trial found no improvement in IVF live births — the evidence is weak or negative.
body.zh: 針灸是中醫裡研究最多的部分。英國 NICE 的指引說，慢性原發性疼痛、預防慢性緊縮型頭痛（以及標準預防藥物無效時的偏頭痛），可以考慮針灸；美國國家輔助與整合健康中心（NCCIH）整理的證據顯示，它可能對下背痛、頸痛、膝關節炎、頭痛有幫助。各家指引並不一致：NICE 自己的下背痛指引就說不要提供針灸。另外還有兩點要誠實說明：很多試驗中，「假針灸」（假針或淺刺）的效果和真針灸差不多，所以效果有多少來自特定穴位，至今仍有爭論；其他許多病症的證據薄弱甚至是負面的，例如生育，一個大型試驗發現針灸並沒有提高試管嬰兒的活產率。

body.en: In trained hands with sterile single-use needles, acupuncture is very safe. Two large UK surveys published in 2001, covering more than 60,000 treatments, found no serious adverse events; minor bruising, soreness, and brief dizziness were the most common problems. Always tell your practitioner if you take blood thinners, are pregnant or trying to conceive, have a pacemaker (no electro-acupuncture), or have a bleeding disorder.
body.zh: 由受過訓練的人、使用無菌拋棄式針具，針灸非常安全。英國 2001 年發表的兩個大型調查，合計六萬多次治療，沒有發現嚴重不良事件；最常見的是輕微瘀青、痠痛和短暫頭暈。如果你在吃抗凝血藥、懷孕或準備懷孕、裝有心律調節器（不能做電針）、或有凝血疾病，一定要告訴醫師。

takeaway.en: Acupuncture is safe in trained hands and reasonably supported for some chronic pain and headaches. Give it a fair trial, stop if nothing changes, and keep your other doctors informed.
takeaway.zh: 針灸在專業人員手上很安全，對某些慢性疼痛和頭痛有一定的證據。給它一次公平的嘗試，沒有變化就停；也要讓你的其他醫師知道。

Why Pressing a Sore Spot Sometimes Helps

q.en: Modern acupuncture needles are…
q.zh: 現代針灸針是……

opts.en: solid, very thin, sterile, and single-use
opts.zh: 實心、很細、無菌、用一次就丟

why.en: About 0.16–0.30 mm, flexible, and disposable.
why.zh: 大約 0.16 到 0.30 公釐，有彈性，拋棄式。

q.en: What do the round marks after cupping represent?
q.zh: 拔罐後的圓形痕跡是什麼？

why.en: They are bruises and fade in several days. "Toxins" is a marketing word, not a finding.
why.zh: 那是瘀血，幾天內會消退。「毒素」是行銷用語，不是研究結果。

q.en: For which conditions do NICE guidelines say acupuncture can be considered?
q.zh: NICE 指引說哪些狀況可以考慮針灸？

opts.en: Chronic primary pain and headache prevention
opts.zh: 慢性原發性疼痛、預防頭痛

why.en: Chronic primary pain and prevention of chronic tension-type headache — though NICE advises against it for low-back pain.
why.zh: 慢性原發性疼痛、預防慢性緊縮型頭痛；不過 NICE 不建議用針灸治下背痛。

q.en: Why is the role of specific points debated?
q.zh: 為什麼「穴位的特定作用」有爭議？

opts.en: Sham acupuncture often does nearly as well in trials
opts.zh: 試驗中假針灸的效果常常差不多

why.en: The overall experience helps some people, but how much depends on exact points is unclear.
why.zh: 整體的治療經驗對一些人有幫助，但有多少取決於精確的穴位，目前還不清楚。

q.en: A patient takes warfarin (a blood thinner). What should they do before acupuncture?
q.zh: 病人在吃抗凝血藥 warfarin，針灸前該怎麼做？

why.en: Treatment is usually still possible with care. Never stop a prescribed drug without the prescribing doctor.
why.zh: 通常仍可以小心治療。沒有開藥醫師的同意，絕對不要自己停藥。

tag.en: Formulas, not single herbs — and why "natural" is not the same as "safe."
tag.zh: 用的是方劑，不是單味藥；以及為什麼「天然」不等於「安全」。

blocks.en: Chinese herbal medicine is TCM's deepest clinical tool, with a written tradition running from the Shennong Bencao Jing (神農本草經, Eastern Han dynasty, 365 substances) to Li Shizhen's great Bencao Gangmu (本草綱目), finished in 1578 and printed in the 1590s. Most substances are plants; some are minerals or animal products.
blocks.zh: 中藥是中醫最深的臨床工具。文字傳統從東漢的《神農本草經》（收藥 365 種），一直到李時珍的《本草綱目》（1578 年完成，1590 年代刊行）。藥材大多是植物，也有礦物和動物來源。

blocks.en: Unlike much Western herbalism, TCM rarely uses one herb alone. It uses formulas (方劑) of several herbs with assigned roles — the "sovereign, minister, assistant, and envoy" (君臣佐使). The sovereign targets the main problem; the minister supports it; the assistant handles side issues or tempers harshness; the envoy guides and harmonizes the whole.
blocks.zh: 和許多西方草藥學不同，中醫很少只用一味藥，而是用好幾味藥組成方劑，各有角色，叫做「君臣佐使」：君藥針對主要問題，臣藥輔助君藥，佐藥處理次要問題或緩和藥性，使藥引導並調和全方。

rows.en: Spleen qi deficiency: tired, poor appetite, loose stools. Ginseng, atractylodes, poria, licorice.
rows.zh: 脾氣虛：倦怠、食慾差、大便稀。人參、白朮、茯苓、甘草。

rows.en: Blood deficiency, especially in women's health.
Song dynasty, Qian Yi, Xiaoer Yaozheng Zhijue
rows.zh: 宋・錢乙《小兒藥證直訣》

body.en: Most Taiwanese TCM clinics prescribe concentrated granules (科學中藥), mixed into hot water and covered by National Health Insurance. Some clinics and traditional pharmacies (中藥行) also prepare decoctions (水煎藥) from raw herbs. Packaged TCM products sold legally in Taiwan carry a Ministry of Health and Welfare permit number on the box.
body.zh: 台灣的中醫診所大多開立科學中藥（濃縮顆粒），用熱水沖服，健保有給付；也有診所和中藥行用生藥材煎煮水煎藥。在台灣合法販售的包裝中藥製劑，盒子上會印有衛生福利部的許可證字號。

blocks.en: Safety: what every reader should know
blocks.zh: 安全：每個人都該知道的事

items.en: Herbs are drugs. Some are toxic. Taiwan banned herbs containing aristolochic acid in 2003 after they were linked to kidney failure and urinary-tract cancers — a lesson in why "traditional" is not proof of safety.
items.zh: 中藥就是藥。有些有毒。台灣在 2003 年禁用含馬兜鈴酸的藥材，因為它們和腎衰竭、泌尿道癌症有關。這說明「傳統」不等於安全的證明。

items.en: Interactions are real. Dong quai (當歸) and danshen (丹參) may raise bleeding risk with warfarin; American ginseng can weaken warfarin's effect. Tell both your TCM physician and your Western doctor everything you take.
items.zh: 交互作用是真的。當歸、丹參可能增加 warfarin 的出血風險；西洋參可能減弱 warfarin 的效果。你吃的每一樣東西，都要讓中醫師和西醫都知道。

items.en: Don't self-prescribe formulas. A tonic for the wrong pattern can make things worse — the tradition itself warns that ginseng for someone with damp-heat can aggravate heat signs.
items.zh: 不要自己抓方子。補藥用錯了證型反而更糟；傳統本身就提醒，濕熱體質的人吃人參，可能讓熱象更嚴重。

items.en: Pregnancy, children, and older adults need a qualified practitioner, not a shopkeeper's suggestion.
items.zh: 孕婦、小孩、長者需要合格的醫師，不是店家的推薦。

items.en: Buy from licensed sources. Avoid unlabeled powders and products sold online with dramatic claims.
items.zh: 從合法管道購買。避開沒有標示的藥粉，以及網路上宣稱神奇療效的產品。

blocks.en: Five kitchen herbs
blocks.zh: 五種廚房裡的藥材

blocks.en: These are classified as both food and medicine and are reasonable for everyday cooking in normal amounts: fresh ginger (生薑), red dates (紅棗), goji berries (枸杞), dried tangerine peel (陳皮), and Chinese yam (山藥). Anything beyond the kitchen — capsules, concentrated extracts, or a formula — is a conversation for a licensed practitioner.
blocks.zh: 這幾種屬於藥食兩用，日常以一般份量入菜是合理的：生薑、紅棗、枸杞、陳皮、山藥。超出廚房範圍的，例如膠囊、濃縮萃取物或方劑，就該找有執照的醫師談。

body.en: The most famous success is artemisinin. In the 1970s Tu Youyou's team found a line in Ge Hong's fourth-century Handbook of Prescriptions for Emergencies (肘後備急方) about soaking sweet wormwood (青蒿) in water, which suggested extracting it without heat; the resulting drug has saved millions from malaria, and she shared the 2015 Nobel Prize. Notice what made it work: modern chemistry, purification, and clinical trials. For most traditional formulas, large high-quality trials are still scarce, and product quality and contamination remain real concerns.
body.zh: 最有名的成功例子是青蒿素。1970 年代，屠呦呦的團隊從葛洪四世紀的《肘後備急方》中讀到用水浸泡青蒿的記載，想到要避免高溫萃取；研發出的藥物救了數百萬瘧疾病人，她也因此共同獲得 2015 年諾貝爾獎。但要注意它成功的關鍵：現代化學、純化和臨床試驗。大部分傳統方劑至今仍缺少大規模高品質的試驗，產品品質和汙染也仍是實際的問題。

takeaway.en: Chinese herbs are real pharmacology: powerful, formula-based, and capable of harm. Cook with kitchen herbs freely; for anything more, see a licensed practitioner and keep your Western doctor informed.
takeaway.zh: 中藥是真正的藥理：有力量、以方劑為主，也可能造成傷害。廚房裡的藥材可以安心入菜；超過這個範圍，請找有執照的醫師，也讓你的西醫知道。

q.en: What does describe?
q.zh: 「君臣佐使」描述的是什麼？

opts.en: The roles of herbs in a formula

why.en: Sovereign, minister, assistant, envoy — each herb has a job.
why.zh: 君、臣、佐、使，每一味藥各有任務。

q.en: Which formula is the classic tonic for Spleen qi deficiency?
q.zh: 哪一個方劑是補脾氣虛的經典方？

why.en: Ginseng, atractylodes, poria, licorice.
why.zh: 人參、白朮、茯苓、甘草。

q.en: Why did Taiwan ban herbs containing aristolochic acid in 2003?
q.zh: 台灣為什麼在 2003 年禁用含馬兜鈴酸的藥材？

opts.en: They were linked to kidney failure and urinary-tract cancer
opts.zh: 和腎衰竭、泌尿道癌症有關

why.en: A clear lesson that "traditional" does not mean safe.
why.zh: 這清楚說明「傳統」不等於安全。

q.en: A friend on warfarin wants to start dong quai. What is the right advice?
q.zh: 朋友在吃 warfarin，想開始吃當歸，該怎麼建議？

opts.en: Talk to both the prescribing doctor and a licensed TCM physician first
opts.zh: 先和開藥的醫師、有執照的中醫師都談過

why.en: Dong quai may raise bleeding risk with warfarin.
why.zh: 當歸和 warfarin 併用可能增加出血風險。

q.en: What made artemisinin a success?
q.zh: 青蒿素成功的關鍵是什麼？

opts.en: A classical clue, followed by modern chemistry and clinical trials
opts.zh: 古籍的線索，加上現代化學和臨床試驗

why.en: Tradition pointed the way; science made it a medicine.
why.zh: 傳統指了方向，科學讓它成為藥物。

tag.en: When to go to the hospital, when TCM may help, and how to choose a practitioner.
tag.zh: 什麼時候該去醫院、什麼時候中醫可能有幫助，以及怎麼挑選醫師。

blocks.en: Self-care from this course is for mild, short-lived things: a tired week, a heavy meal, a stiff neck, seasonal adjustments. Anything more benefits from a professional — Western, TCM, or both.
blocks.zh: 這門課的自我保健，適用於輕微、短暫的狀況：累了一週、吃得太撐、脖子僵硬、季節轉換的調整。超過這些，就該找專業人員：西醫、中醫，或兩者都看。

blocks.en: Red flags: go to the hospital first
blocks.zh: 危險徵兆：先去醫院

blocks.en: In Taiwan, call 119 for an ambulance. Do not delay any of these with herbs, acupressure, or waiting to see.
blocks.zh: 在台灣，叫救護車請打 119。以下情況都不要用中藥、按穴位或「再觀察看看」來拖延。

items.en: Chest pain or pressure, especially spreading to the arm, jaw, or back
items.zh: 胸痛或胸悶，尤其痛到手臂、下巴或背部

items.en: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side, a drooping face, slurred speech, or confusion (possible stroke)
items.zh: 突然一側無力或麻木、臉歪、說話不清、意識混亂（可能是中風）

items.en: Severe difficulty breathing, or blue lips
items.zh: 嚴重呼吸困難，或嘴唇發紫

items.en: Vomiting blood, black or bloody stools
items.zh: 吐血、黑便或血便

items.en: A sudden, "worst-ever" headache
items.zh: 突然發生、「這輩子最痛」的頭痛

items.en: High fever that will not come down, or any fever in a baby under three months
items.zh: 退不下來的高燒，或三個月以下嬰兒發燒

items.en: Severe or worsening abdominal pain
items.zh: 劇烈或越來越嚴重的腹痛

items.en: Swelling of the face or throat after a food, drug, or sting
items.zh: 吃了食物、藥物或被叮咬後，臉部或喉嚨腫起來

items.en: Thoughts of suicide or harming yourself — in Taiwan you can also call the 1925 mental-health line, any time
items.zh: 想要自殺或傷害自己——在台灣也可以隨時撥打 1925 安心專線

items.en: Unexplained weight loss, or a lump that is growing or changing
items.zh: 原因不明的體重減輕，或持續長大、變化的腫塊

blocks.en: Where TCM is often used
blocks.zh: 中醫常被使用的領域

blocks.en: People commonly seek TCM for chronic pain, headaches, digestive complaints without a structural cause, sleep and stress, menstrual pain and menopausal symptoms, allergic rhinitis, and support during recovery from illness or cancer treatment. The strength of evidence differs across this list (Module 10), so it is reasonable to agree on a trial period and a clear sign of improvement before you start.
blocks.zh: 大家常為了這些找中醫：慢性疼痛、頭痛、沒有器質性原因的腸胃不適、睡眠與壓力、經痛與更年期症狀、過敏性鼻炎，以及病後或癌症治療期間的調養。這些項目的證據強弱不一（見第十單元），所以開始之前，和醫師約定一段嘗試期、以及怎樣才算改善，是合理的做法。

blocks.en: Choosing a practitioner
blocks.zh: 怎麼挑選中醫師

items.en: In Taiwan, a 中醫師 holds a national license; clinics display it. Outside Taiwan, look for your country's or state's licensure — in the United States, many states require NCCAOM certification.
items.zh: 在台灣，中醫師持有國家證照，診所會公開展示。在台灣以外，請確認當地的執照制度；例如美國，許多州要求 NCCAOM 認證。

items.en: Ask what they think is going on, what the treatment plan is, how long before you should expect change, and what it costs.
items.zh: 問醫師：你認為我是什麼狀況？治療計畫是什麼？多久應該看到變化？費用多少？

items.en: A good practitioner is comfortable working with your other doctors and asks what medicines you take.
items.zh: 好的醫師願意和你的其他醫師合作，也會主動問你在吃哪些藥。

body.en: Walk away from anyone who tells you to stop a prescribed medicine, claims to cure cancer or diabetes with herbs alone, discourages you from seeing other doctors, sells expensive prepaid packages under pressure, or will not show credentials.
body.zh: 遇到以下情況就離開：叫你停掉醫師開的藥、宣稱只用中藥就能治好癌症或糖尿病、勸你不要看其他醫生、強迫推銷昂貴的預付療程，或不肯出示證照。

title.en: The principle that ties it together
title.zh: 把這一切串起來的原則

body.en: Use Western medicine for diagnosis, emergencies, and structural problems. Consider TCM for chronic patterns, recovery, and daily habits — and judge it by results. Above all, tell each practitioner what the other is doing. Hidden parallel treatment is where most real harm comes from: herb–drug interactions and delayed diagnoses.
body.zh: 診斷、急症和結構性問題，交給西醫；慢性體質、復原期和日常生活習慣，可以考慮中醫，並且用結果來判斷它。最重要的是：讓每一位醫師都知道另一位在做什麼。多數真正的傷害都來自彼此不知情的並行治療：中西藥交互作用，以及延誤診斷。

takeaway.en: Acute and serious: hospital first. Chronic and constitutional: TCM may be worth a fair trial. Always: tell every clinician about every other one.
takeaway.zh: 急性、嚴重的：先去醫院。慢性、體質性的：中醫或許值得公平地試一試。永遠記得：讓每一位醫師都知道其他醫師的治療。

q.en: Sudden weakness on one side and slurred speech call for…
q.zh: 突然一側無力、說話不清，應該……

why.en: Possible stroke. Treatment within hours can prevent permanent damage.
why.zh: 可能是中風。數小時內治療可以避免永久傷害。

q.en: A practitioner tells you to stop your blood-pressure medicine and take their herbs instead. This is…
q.zh: 醫師叫你停掉降血壓藥，改吃他的中藥，這是……

opts.en: Fine if the herbs are organic
opts.zh: 如果中藥是有機的就沒問題

why.en: Stopping blood-pressure medicine suddenly can be dangerous. Find another practitioner.
why.zh: 突然停掉降血壓藥可能很危險。換一位醫師。

q.en: What is the best first question when choosing a TCM clinic outside Taiwan?
q.zh: 在台灣以外挑選中醫診所，最該先問什麼？

opts.en: Are you licensed, and may I see your credentials?
opts.zh: 你有執照嗎？可以讓我看看證書嗎？

why.en: Licensure is the basic safeguard everywhere TCM is regulated.
why.zh: 在有管理中醫的地方，執照都是最基本的保障。

q.en: Where does most real harm from combining the two systems come from?
q.zh: 兩套醫學並用時，真正的傷害大多來自哪裡？

opts.en: Hidden parallel treatment: interactions and delayed diagnosis
opts.zh: 彼此不知情的並行治療：交互作用和延誤診斷

why.en: Tell every clinician what the others are doing.
why.zh: 讓每一位醫師都知道其他醫師在做什麼。

signs.en: I usually have steady energy through the day.
signs.zh: 我一天的精神大多很穩定。

signs.en: I sleep well and my appetite is regular.
signs.zh: 我睡得好，胃口規律。

signs.en: I adapt easily to hot or cold weather.
signs.zh: 我對冷熱天氣都適應得不錯。

about.en: The reference type: steady energy, good sleep and digestion, adapts well.
about.zh: 作為參照的體質：精神穩定、睡眠消化都好、適應力強。

advice.en: Traditional advice: keep what works — regular meals, regular sleep, moderate exercise.
advice.zh: 傳統建議：維持現在有效的習慣，三餐定時、作息規律、適度運動。

signs.en: I get tired easily, even after an ordinary day.
signs.zh: 平常的一天也容易累。

signs.en: I get short of breath when climbing stairs, and my voice is soft.
signs.zh: 爬樓梯容易喘，說話聲音小。

signs.en: I sweat easily without much effort and catch colds often.
signs.zh: 稍微動一下就出汗，常感冒。

about.en: Low working capacity: fatigue, breathlessness, frequent colds.
about.zh: 氣不足：容易疲倦、氣短、常感冒。

advice.en: Traditional advice: warm, regular meals (rice, yam, sweet potato, red dates); gentle movement like walking or tai chi rather than exhausting workouts.
advice.zh: 傳統建議：溫熱、定時的飲食（米飯、山藥、地瓜、紅棗）；散步、太極這類溫和運動，不要累到透支。

signs.en: My hands and feet are cold, even in mild weather.
signs.zh: 天氣不冷，手腳也冰冷。

signs.en: I prefer hot drinks; cold or raw food upsets my stomach.
signs.zh: 我喜歡熱飲；吃冰的、生的容易不舒服。

signs.en: I feel the cold more than people around me.
signs.zh: 我比身邊的人怕冷。

about.en: Not enough warming: cold limbs, prefers warmth, sluggish digestion.
about.zh: 溫煦不足：手腳冰冷、喜溫、消化較慢。

advice.en: Traditional advice: cooked, warming food (ginger, scallion, cinnamon, walnuts, leeks); avoid iced drinks; keep the lower back and belly warm.
advice.zh: 傳統建議：吃煮熟、溫性的食物（薑、蔥、肉桂、核桃、韭菜）；避免冰飲；腰腹保暖。

signs.en: My palms and soles often feel hot.
signs.zh: 手心腳心常常發熱。

signs.en: My mouth and throat are dry, especially at night.
signs.zh: 口乾咽乾，夜裡更明顯。

signs.en: I sleep restlessly and sometimes sweat at night.
signs.zh: 睡得不安穩，有時夜裡出汗。

about.en: Not enough cooling and moistening: heat in the palms, dryness, restless sleep.
about.zh: 涼潤不足：手足心熱、乾燥、睡不安穩。

advice.en: Traditional advice: moistening food (pear, white fungus, lily bulb, black sesame, tofu); go easy on spicy and fried food, alcohol, and late nights.
advice.zh: 傳統建議：多吃滋潤的食物（梨、白木耳、百合、黑芝麻、豆腐）；少吃辛辣油炸、少喝酒、別熬夜。

signs.en: My body often feels heavy, as if weighed down.
signs.zh: 身體常覺得沉重，像被壓著。

signs.en: My belly is soft and full, and I put on weight easily.
signs.zh: 腹部鬆軟肥滿，容易發胖。

signs.en: My mouth feels sticky, or I often have phlegm in my throat.
signs.zh: 嘴裡黏黏的，或喉嚨常有痰。

about.en: Fluids not moving well: heaviness, weight gain, phlegm.
about.zh: 水濕運化不好：身重、易胖、多痰。

advice.en: Traditional advice: lighter food (job's tears, adzuki beans, white radish, tangerine peel); less sugar, dairy, and fried food; daily exercise.
advice.zh: 傳統建議：清淡的飲食（薏仁、紅豆、白蘿蔔、陳皮）；少糖、少奶製品、少油炸；每天運動。

signs.en: My face and nose get oily, and I break out easily.
signs.zh: 臉和鼻子容易出油、長痘。

signs.en: I often have a bitter taste in my mouth.
signs.zh: 常常覺得口苦。

signs.en: My stools are sticky, or my urine is dark.
signs.zh: 大便黏滯，或小便顏色深。

about.en: Dampness combined with heat: oily skin, breakouts, bitter mouth.
about.zh: 濕與熱結合：皮膚油、長痘、口苦。

advice.en: Traditional advice: cooling, draining food (mung beans, bitter melon, cucumber, winter melon); avoid alcohol, fried food, and heavy spicy meals.
advice.zh: 傳統建議：清熱利濕的食物（綠豆、苦瓜、小黃瓜、冬瓜）；避免喝酒、油炸、重辣。

signs.en: My complexion is dull, or I have dark circles under my eyes.
signs.zh: 臉色晦暗，或有黑眼圈。

signs.en: I bruise easily without knowing why.
signs.zh: 常不知不覺出現瘀青。

signs.en: I have pains that stay in one fixed place.
signs.zh: 有固定在同一個地方的疼痛。

about.en: Blood not moving freely: dull complexion, easy bruising, fixed pain.
about.zh: 血行不暢：膚色晦暗、易瘀青、痛有定處。

advice.en: Traditional advice: keep moving and avoid sitting for long periods; black fungus, hawthorn, and a little vinegar in cooking.
advice.zh: 傳統建議：多活動、避免久坐；料理中可用黑木耳、山楂、少許醋。

signs.en: I sigh a lot, or my chest feels tight when I'm stressed.
signs.zh: 常嘆氣，壓力大時胸口悶。

signs.en: My mood goes up and down easily.
signs.zh: 情緒容易起伏。

signs.en: I sometimes feel something stuck in my throat.
signs.zh: 有時覺得喉嚨卡著東西。

about.en: Qi not flowing smoothly: sighing, mood swings, tightness with stress.
about.zh: 氣機不暢：嘆氣、情緒起伏、壓力大時悶脹。

advice.en: Traditional advice: regular exercise, time outdoors, and someone to talk to; rose or jasmine tea and citrus peel. If low mood lasts more than two weeks, see a doctor.
advice.zh: 傳統建議：規律運動、到戶外走走、找人聊聊；玫瑰花茶、茉莉花茶、陳皮。情緒低落超過兩週，請看醫生。

signs.en: I have allergies to pollen, dust, or certain foods.
signs.zh: 我對花粉、塵蟎或某些食物過敏。

signs.en: I sneeze or get a runny nose even without a cold.
signs.zh: 沒感冒也常打噴嚏、流鼻水。

signs.en: My skin reacts easily — hives, itching, or rashes.
signs.zh: 皮膚容易起反應，例如蕁麻疹、癢、紅疹。

about.en: A sensitive constitution: allergies, hay fever, reactive skin.
about.zh: 敏感的體質：過敏、過敏性鼻炎、皮膚容易起反應。

advice.en: Traditional advice: identify and avoid triggers, avoid sudden temperature changes, and don't experiment with "immune-boosting" herbs on your own. Known allergies should be managed with your doctor.
advice.zh: 傳統建議：找出並避開過敏原、避免溫差太大，不要自己嘗試「增強免疫」的藥材。已知的過敏要和醫師一起處理。

note.zh: 清熱，濕熱天氣的經典食材。

note.en: Moistens the intestines.
Mung bean soup is Taiwan's summer classic.
note.zh: 綠豆湯是台灣夏天的經典。

note.en: Salty and cooling.
Traditionally not eaten on an empty stomach.

Cooling; less so when stir-fried.
Drains dampness; a summer soup.
Moistens the Lung; stewed pear for a dry autumn cough.
Often cooked with ginger or scallion.
Said to calm Liver heat.
Cook lightly.
Helps with food stagnation and phlegm.
Sources differ; cooking makes it milder.
note.zh: 各家說法不一；煮過較溫和。

note.en: Cooler than black or oolong tea.
Sources differ (neutral or cool); drink it warm.
note.zh: 各家說法不一（平或涼）；溫熱喝。

note.en: The everyday staple; supports the Spleen.
Supports digestion.
A gentle tonic for Spleen, Lung, and Kidney.

Drains dampness gently.
Traditionally nourishes the Kidney.

Moistens dryness; a classic dessert soup.
Moistens the Lung and calms the mind.
Nourishing for most people.

note.zh: 各家說法不一（平或微寒）。

note.en: Moistening; not for babies under one year.
note.zh: 潤燥；一歲以下嬰兒不可食用。

note.en: Mildly tonifying.
A savory everyday ingredient.
The most useful warming ingredient in the kitchen.
note.zh: 廚房裡最好用的溫性食材。

note.en: Used at the very start of a cold with chills.
Strongly warming; use moderately.
Traditionally warms yang.
Gently warming; supports digestion.
Tonifying but heavy; don't overeat.
note.zh: 補益但難消化，別吃太多。

note.en: Traditionally warms the Kidney and lower back.
Nourishes the Heart; very warming dried.
note.zh: 養心；乾的龍眼乾溫性更強。

note.en: An everyday gentle tonic.
Strongly warming; cinnamon bark is classed as hot.
Warm brown-sugar ginger tea is a familiar remedy for period cramps.
note.zh: 黑糖薑茶是常見的經痛飲品。

note.en: Warmer than green tea.
Aids digestion.
Sources differ on the raw oil; cooked with ginger and rice wine in 麻油雞, it is treated as strongly warming.
note.zh: 生油的性質各家說法不一；在麻油雞裡和薑、米酒一起煮，被視為溫性很強。

note.en: A classic food for recovery.
Strongly warming; a winter food.
Strongly heating; avoid if you run hot.
note.zh: 熱性強；體質偏熱的人少吃。

note.en: Warms the middle.
Numbing and warming.
In the tradition: deep breathing, the end of sleep.
note.zh: 傳統：呼吸深沉，睡眠將盡。

note.en: In the tradition: rise, drink warm water, empty the bowels.
In the tradition: the best time for a warm breakfast.
note.zh: 傳統：吃一頓溫熱早餐的最好時間。

note.en: In the tradition: digestion turns breakfast into nourishment; good for focused work.
note.zh: 傳統：早餐化為養分；適合專注工作。

note.en: In the tradition: a light lunch and a short rest.
note.zh: 傳統：午餐清淡、小憩片刻。

note.en: In the tradition: sorting the clear from the turbid.
In the tradition: drink water and move.
In the tradition: ease off; a lighter dinner.
note.zh: 傳統：放慢腳步；晚餐清淡。

note.en: In the tradition: calm time with family and friends.
note.zh: 傳統：和家人朋友輕鬆相處。

note.en: In the tradition: wind down and prepare for sleep.
In the tradition: already asleep.
In the tradition: deep sleep; the Liver stores blood.

loc.en: On the back of the hand, in the fleshy web between the thumb and index finger, beside the middle of the second hand bone.
loc.zh: 手背，拇指和食指之間的虎口肉上，靠近第二掌骨中點。

use.en: Traditionally used for headache, toothache, and facial pain.
use.zh: 傳統用於頭痛、牙痛、顏面疼痛。

loc.en: On the inner forearm, 2 cun (about three finger-widths) above the wrist crease, between the two tendons.
loc.zh: 前臂內側，腕橫紋上 2 寸（約三橫指），兩條肌腱之間。

use.en: Nausea, motion sickness, and nausea after surgery — the best-supported point.
use.zh: 噁心、暈車，以及手術後的噁心；研究證據最好的穴位。

loc.en: On the front of the lower leg, 3 cun (four finger-widths) below the kneecap's outer hollow, one finger-width outside the shinbone.
loc.zh: 小腿前外側，外膝眼（犢鼻）下 3 寸（四橫指），脛骨前緣外一橫指。

use.en: The classic "everyday" point for digestion and fatigue in the tradition.
use.zh: 傳統上調理消化與疲倦的「保健要穴」。

loc.en: On the inner lower leg, 3 cun (four finger-widths) above the tip of the inner ankle bone, just behind the shinbone.
loc.zh: 小腿內側，內踝尖上 3 寸（四橫指），脛骨內側緣後方。

use.en: Traditionally used for menstrual pain, digestion, and sleep.
use.zh: 傳統用於經痛、消化、睡眠。

loc.en: On the top of the foot, in the hollow between the first and second toe bones, just before they meet.
loc.zh: 足背，第一、第二蹠骨之間，兩骨交會處前方的凹陷。

use.en: Traditionally used for stress, irritability, and headache; often paired with LI4 as the "Four Gates."
use.zh: 傳統用於壓力、煩躁、頭痛；常和合谷合稱「四關」。
